login.title: Sign in
login.subtitle: Sign in to manage your home services
login.name: User name
login.throttled: Too many attempts. Try again in {seconds} s.
login.failed: Could not sign in. Check that the portal is reachable.

dashboard.title: Home
dashboard.subtitle: The state of your home services
dashboard.unknownWidget: This version of the interface does not support the “{type}” widget
dashboard.invalidWidget: The settings of the “{type}” widget are invalid

services.title: Services
services.emptyHint: Add the first service on the “Services” page.

calendar.title: Calendar
calendar.emptyHint: The calendar returned no events for the next few days.
calendar.unsupportedRepeat: This repeat rule is not supported: only the next event is shown.

services.title: Services
services.subtitle: The services the portal shows and checks
services.emptyHint: Add a service: it will appear on the home page and start being checked.
services.deleteDescription: The service will be removed from the configuration and will no longer be checked.

serviceForm.description: Changes are written to the configuration file.
serviceForm.idHint: Lower-case Latin letters, digits and hyphens, for example jellyfin
serviceForm.name: Name
serviceForm.urlHint: http or https, for example http://192.168.1.10:8096
serviceForm.iconHint: A lucide name (server, film), auto for the service's own icon, catalog:jellyfin, url:… or file:…

probeKindHints.http: An HTTP request to the address and path; for web interfaces
probeKindHints.tcp: A connection to the port; for SSH, SMB, printers and other non-HTTP services
probeKindHints.icmp: An echo request (ping); only whether the host answers

serviceForm.probePortHint: When empty, the port from the address or the scheme's default (ssh: 22)
serviceForm.notesHint: Markdown is supported; shown on the service page
serviceForm.groupHint: Choose an existing group or type a new one
serviceForm.iconPreview: This is how the icon will look
serviceForm.leave: The service has unsaved changes. Leave the page?
serviceForm.notFoundHint: It may have been deleted or renamed.
serviceForm.publicationDescription: The address Caddy serves this service at, and who has to sign in to the portal for it
serviceForm.publicationDisabled: The proxy is off: the publication is kept in the configuration and starts working when the proxy is switched on.
serviceForm.publicationHostHint: A host name, for example media.example.com. Leave empty to not publish.
serviceForm.publicationUpstreamHint: By default, the address the service is checked at
serviceForm.publicationEnvironments: Show this address in the environments
serviceForm.publicationAuth: Require signing in to the portal from the environments

publicationTlsHints.acme: Needs ports 80 and 443 forwarded to Caddy
publicationTlsHints.internal: For addresses that exist only inside; the root certificate is on the “Proxy” page
publicationTlsHints.files: Paths to files on the machine Caddy runs on

network.title: Network
network.subtitle: Where the portal listens and how it is found on the network
network.effectiveAddress: The address the portal listens on now
network.overridden: The address is set by the HOME_PORTAL_ADDRESS environment variable: the settings below apply only once it is removed.
network.restartRequired: The settings are saved. They take effect after the portal restarts.
network.addressHint: 0.0.0.0 to listen on every interface, 127.0.0.1 for this machine only
network.publicUrlHint: How the portal is opened in a browser, for example https://portal.home.lan
network.trustedProxiesHint: One per line: an IP address or a range, for example 10.0.0.0/8
network.interfacesHint: This machine's addresses, for reference only

errors.conflict: The configuration was changed elsewhere. The data has been reloaded: check it and save again. What you typed has been kept.

validation.id: Lower-case Latin letters, digits and hyphens only; starts with a letter; up to 63 characters
validation.name: From 1 to 80 characters
validation.url: An absolute address is needed: http or https for an HTTP probe, any address with a host for TCP and ICMP
validation.probeTimeout: From 1 to 60 seconds, and less than the interval
validation.address: An IP address is needed, for example 0.0.0.0 or 192.168.1.10
validation.publicUrl: An absolute http or https address is needed
validation.trustedProxy: An IP address or a CIDR range is needed
validation.probePort: Give a port from 1 to 65535, in the address or in the probe settings
validation.linkUrl: An absolute http or https address is needed
validation.proxyHost: A host name is needed: lower-case Latin letters, digits, hyphens and dots, with no scheme or port
validation.proxyUpstream: An absolute http or https address is needed
validation.proxyUpstreamRequired: Give an http or https address: the service is not checked over HTTP
validation.proxyEnvironments: Only the environments the service is shown in can be chosen
validation.proxyAddressGiven: The service already has its own address for this environment
validation.proxyPortalHostRequired: Give the portal's address: the proxy cannot be switched on without it
validation.proxyCookieDomain: Must be the portal's address or a parent domain of it
validation.caddySource: An https address is needed, or http on this machine (127.0.0.1, localhost)
validation.caddyVersion: latest or an exact version, for example 2.10.2
validation.proxySamePorts: The HTTP and HTTPS ports must differ

environment.label: Environment
environment.explains: The portal worked out your environment from your address and shows the services' addresses for it.
environment.lookFrom: View the portal as from the environment
environment.viewingAs: Viewing as from “{environment}”; you are in “{detected}”

publicPortal.emptyHint: The portal's owner has not marked any service as open yet.

home.empty: The home page is empty for now
home.emptyHint: Add widgets and arrange them in sections in the layout editor.

local-network-denied.title: No access to the local network
local-network-denied.action: macOS has denied the portal access to the local network. Allow it in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Local Network for the application that runs the portal (the terminal, or the portal itself when launchd runs it), then check again.

refused.title: Connection refused
refused.action: The host answered, but nothing listens on this port. Check the port and that the service is running.

timeout.title: No answer
timeout.action: No answer came in time. The host may be off, a firewall may be dropping the packets, or the timeout may be too short.

host-unreachable.title: Host unreachable
host-unreachable.action: There is no route to the host. Check that it is on and on a network this machine can reach.

name-not-resolved.title: Name not found
name-not-resolved.action: The host name does not resolve. Check the spelling and this machine's DNS server.

tls.title: TLS error
tls.action: A TLS connection could not be made. The service may use plain http, or its certificate is not trusted.

not-http.title: Not an HTTP answer
not-http.action: The service answered, but not over HTTP. Check the port or use a TCP probe.

http-status.title: The service answered with an error
http-status.action: Look at the service's logs, or set the probe path to a page that answers 200.

icmp-not-permitted.title: ICMP not permitted
icmp-not-permitted.action: The process may not send ICMP requests. On Linux, allow its group in net.ipv4.ping_group_range, or use a TCP probe.

other.title: The check failed
other.action: The details are in the error text.

probeNow.throttled: Too often: try again in {seconds} s
probeNow.disabled: Checking is off in the service's settings

servicePage.notFoundHint: There is no such service, or it is not shown in your environment.

addresses.title: Addresses
addresses.description: The address depends on the network the portal is opened from.

history.title: History
history.noSamples: There were no checks in this period

transitions.title: State changes
transitions.empty: The state did not change in this period

servicePage.duration: {days, plural, =0 {} other {# d }}{hours, plural, =0 {} other {# h }}{minutes} min

layoutEditor.title: Home page layout
layoutEditor.subtitle: The home page is split into sections. Widgets in a section run left to right and wrap when a row is full. Drag a widget by its handle to change its order and section, and drag its right edge (or use the arrow keys on it) to change its width. On a phone every widget takes the full width.
layoutEditor.examples: Example layouts are in the examples/ folder next to the program.
layoutEditor.leave: Leave the page? Unsaved layout changes will be lost.
layoutEditor.conflict: The configuration file changed while you were editing. Your layout is still on screen.
layoutEditor.reload: Load the layout from the file
layoutEditor.invalid: The layout cannot be saved: fix the marked fields.
layoutEditor.emptySection: Drag a widget here or add a new one
layoutEditor.removeDescription: The widget disappears from the home page once the layout is saved.
layoutEditor.unknownType: This version of the interface does not know the type “{type}”: it can be moved and removed, and its settings stay as they are in the file.
layoutEditor.widgetTitleHint: Leave empty for this type's default title
layoutEditor.environmentsHint: Nothing ticked: the widget is visible in every environment
layoutEditor.publicHint: Guests of the home page will see the widget too, in the ticked environments
layoutEditor.settingsInFile: The settings of this type can only be set in the configuration file for now.
layoutEditor.previewEmpty: The home page has nothing to show this visitor

announce.over: The widget “{title}” is over position {position} in the section “{section}”.
announce.end: The widget “{title}” was dropped at position {position} in the section “{section}”.
announce.instructions: To pick up a widget, press Space or Enter. Move it with the arrow keys, drop it with Space or Enter, or press Escape to cancel.

section.end: The section “{title}” was dropped at position {position}.

widgetSettings.timezone: Time zone, offset from UTC (for example +03:00)
widgetSettings.secret: Secret holding the password or token
widgetSettings.timezoneRule: An offset such as +03:00 is needed
widgetSettings.urlRule: An absolute http or https address is needed
widgetSettings.zone: Time zone (for example Europe/Riga or auto)

proxy.title: Proxy
proxy.subtitle: Publishing services through Caddy: addresses, signing in through the portal, and certificates
proxy.disabled: The proxy is off. Switch it on in the settings below: give the portal's address and save.
proxy.inSync: Running and holding the current configuration
proxy.outOfSync: Reachable, but the current configuration is not applied yet
proxy.applied: The configuration was loaded into Caddy
proxy.rootCertificateHint: Addresses with the local CA are signed by Caddy's own certificate authority. Download its root certificate and install it on your device as trusted, and the browser will stop warning.

caddyControl.title: Caddy
caddyControl.description: The portal can download Caddy itself and keep it running. Caddy runs as a separate process and keeps running when the portal restarts.
caddyControl.external: not the portal: started separately, or not running
caddyControl.unknownOrigin: unknown: downloaded before the portal started recording it, or placed by hand
caddyControl.unsupported: Caddy cannot be downloaded for this machine
caddyControl.verificationNote: The archive is checked against the SHA-512 in the release's checksum file; nothing is installed if it does not match
caddyControl.sourceHint: A GitHub-style releases API: GitHub, Gitea or Forgejo. For example https://api.github.com/repos/caddyserver/caddy/releases
caddyControl.versionHint: latest or an exact version, for example 2.10.2. A new version starts working after Caddy restarts
caddyControl.logHint: Caddy is not answering. The last lines of its log:

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: The [proxy] section of the configuration. Changes take effect at once, without restarting the portal.
settings.portalHostHint: The name Caddy publishes the portal itself under, for example portal.home.example.com
settings.cookieDomainHint: One sign-in covers every address under this domain. Needed when services require signing in through the portal.
settings.loopbackHint: When switched on, the portal adds 127.0.0.1 to the trusted proxies itself: Caddy reaches the portal from that address.
settings.httpsPortHint: Where Caddy accepts https; 443 by default. Another port appears in every address: https://name:port
settings.httpPortHint: For redirecting to https and for the Let's Encrypt check; 80 by default. Let's Encrypt knocks on port 80 from outside, so forward it to this port
